The '''Solaran Parliament''' is the national legislature of [[Solara]] and the central institution of its parliamentary democratic system.

== Constitutional Role ==

Solara was established in 1538 after the [[Grand Duchy of Solan]] and the [[Kingdom of Congrave]] defeated the [[Kingdom of Albion]] in the [[Solaran War of Unification]] and formed a new parliamentary state. The extracted source describes the modern state as a parliamentary democracy with a large legislature of more than 300 representatives.

This draft preserves the parliamentary character of the state while leaving the chamber structure, electoral law, party system, and exact constitutional offices for a later Solaran government pass.

The selection of [[John "Lee" Greener]] as first [[President of Solara]] shows that the founding settlement included a national executive office alongside the representative system. The precise relationship between the early presidency and parliament still needs confirmation.

== Language Reform ==

The parliament is source-attested as the body that commissioned the [[Solaran Alphabet|Sunline]] alphabet in 1895 through the [[Education Reform Act of 1895]]. This made language reform a state-building project rather than only a scholarly preference.

The reform helped move Solara from elite classical literacy toward mass public literacy while preserving [[Solra]] for ceremonial and specialist use.

== National Integration ==

Parliamentary backing gave the reform national legitimacy. The language project connected the state, education system, publishers, provincial schools, and public administration to a common written standard.

The same national confidence later shaped Solara's public identity before the [[Solara-Khalindar War]]. By the early 1990s, Solara saw itself as a modern, literate, unified parliamentary power.

== Canon Notes ==

The source names specific later political leaders and 2000-era demographic/economic data. Those are outside this 1994-back draft batch and should be reviewed in a later modern Solara pass.
